description: A three-column composite of EBSD maps, each column pairing an inverse pole figure (IPF) orientation map (upper panel) with its corresponding phase map (lower panel). Column (a) is the 15Al alloy: the IPF map uses the standard IPF colour triangle inset labelled 001 (top apex), 101 (left) and 111 (right), shows a few very large grains (tens to hundreds of µm) in purple, yellow, orange, pink and cyan, and carries a 500 µm scale bar; its phase map is uniformly red. Column (b) is the 17Al alloy: the IPF map is dominated by a large green grain with blue, purple, cyan and orange neighbours, with a 200 µm scale bar; its phase map is uniformly red. Column (c) is the 19Al alloy: the IPF map shows a much finer, equiaxed, multi-coloured grain structure, with a 500 µm scale bar; its phase map is uniformly red. A legend in every column defines red = α (BCC) and cyan = γ (FCC). The figure demonstrates that the solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels of all three Al contents are single-phase α (BCC) — no γ (FCC) region is resolved in any phase map — and that raising Al from 15 to 19 at.% markedly refines the grain structure. No numeric orientation, grain-size or phase-fraction values are printed on any panel.

subfigures.description: IPF orientation map of the solution-treated 15Al alloy with an inset IPF colour triangle (001/101/111) and a 500 µm scale bar; a small number of very coarse grains in purple, yellow, orange, pink and cyan. Below it, the corresponding phase map is entirely red.

IPF orientation map of the solution-treated 17Al alloy with an inset IPF colour triangle (001/101/111) and a 200 µm scale bar; one dominant green grain surrounded by blue, purple, cyan and orange grains. Below it, the corresponding phase map is entirely red.

IPF orientation map of the solution-treated 19Al alloy with an inset IPF colour triangle (001/101/111) and a 500 µm scale bar; a fine, equiaxed, multi-coloured (red, green, blue, magenta, yellow) grain structure. Below it, the corresponding phase map is entirely red.

observations.observation: Each of the three columns contains an EBSD IPF orientation map above and its corresponding phase map below, sharing the same field of view.
Every phase map is uniformly red across the whole field, and the legend defines red as α (BCC) while cyan is γ (FCC); no cyan region is visible in any of the three phase maps.
The IPF maps carry an inset inverse-pole-figure colour triangle with the corners labelled 001 (top), 101 (lower left) and 111 (lower right).
Scale bars are printed as 500 µm in panel (a), 200 µm in panel (b) and 500 µm in panel (c).
The grain structure coarsens from (c) to (a): panel (c) (19Al) shows fine equiaxed grains while panel (a) (15Al) shows only a handful of very large grains.
The caption states that the panels are the solution-treated (a) 15Al, (b) 17Al and (c) 19Al alloys.
The citing text asserts that the EBSD results of Fig. 3 demonstrate a single α (BCC) phase formed in the solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels.
No numeric orientation values, grain sizes or phase fractions are printed on any panel of the figure.
The legend box in each column lists exactly two phases: α (BCC) in red and γ (FCC) in cyan.

unreadable_items: No numeric grain-size, misorientation or phase-fraction values are legible on any panel because none are printed.
The colour-to-orientation mapping of the individual IPF maps cannot be converted to specific Euler angles or Miller indices from the supplied resolution.
